data.claim: Before the fix none exists: GateOutcome.satisfies is true only for passed (or skipped when not required), chore skips excepted; --force is the only override. A person-held approval by digest (services.approval) can settle one recorded partial without rewriting it to passed.
data.falsifier: A test where a partial required gate completes without a person approval, or where an approval of an earlier outcome settles a later one.
data.mechanism: completion._unsettled counts a gate settled if GateOutcome.settled; add an approval check keyed on item+gate and a digest of the recorded outcome (at, reason); approval.grant refuses agent identities.
data.probe: uv run pytest tests/test_accept_partial_gate.py (unfixed: approve refuses 'not a human-approval gate'; fixed: 5 pass)
data.question: Is there a legitimate, non-forgeable way for a required gate recorded partial to settle complete?

evidence.note: checked r-reuse-core (reuses services.approval + chore pattern, no second engine), r-small-files (new module 2.5KB), r-everything-configurable (no new tunable), D-chore-class/D-test-domains/D-shared-engines-r2 waiver-through-approvals

chunk_findings.detail: The new branch `or (state is not None and GA.accepted(state, it, g).ok)` settles **any** accepted required gate, including a partial `unit_tests` on a code item. This violates operator decision `D-docs-gates-not-applicable` in the intent: code items still need a passed `unit_tests`. Concrete input: a code task such as `fix-B1bfcaf6ebb` changes `.py` files, `unit_tests` is required and recorded as `partial` (`GA.ACCEPTABLE`); after `ddflow approve fix-B1bfcaf6ebb unit_tests`, `_unsettled` removes `unit_tests` from `missing` even though `it.gate_satisfied('unit_tests', True)` is still false. `_accepted_warnings` only appends a warning, so `complete` has no blocker and accepts the code item with `unit_tests` never passed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion.py:_unsettled

chunk_findings.detail: Given a code item whose required non-human gate `unit_tests` is recorded `GA.ACCEPTABLE` (partial), `_clear_gate` now lets a person call accept on it, and `_gates` then excludes that gate from `required_bad` because it appears in the `accepted` sequence. `ddflow complete` therefore stops demanding a passed `unit_tests` for that code item and proceeds with only a WARN. This violates the operator decision in the intent, D-docs-gates-not-applicable: code items still need a passed `unit_tests`; only all-docs items may record `unit_tests` as not-applicable, and the general partial-required-gate case was explicitly left open, not approved for code items.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify.py:_gates and ddflow/services/gates/outcomes.py clear/accept path

chunk_findings.detail: The test and the acceptance path it exercises create a code task (`T1` with `--globs a.py`), record the required `unit_tests` gate as `partial`, approve that partial gate, and then assert `ddflow complete T1` exits 0. This violates the operator decision cited in the intent, [D-docs-gates-not-applicable]: code items still need a `passed` `unit_tests`; only all-docs items may settle `unit_tests`/`ci` as not-applicable, and the general partial-required-gate case is explicitly left open. The change would therefore allow a code item to complete with partial tests instead of requiring a real full-suite pass or merge-queue/full-run outcome.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_accept_partial_gate.py: test_a_person_can_accept_a_partial_required_gate_and_complete_follows

data.body:
Bug Bb999d5e20f is blocked on policy, not code. D-docs-gates-not-applicable (operator, 2026-10-19) settled docs-only items and says: 'Any item that changes code still needs a genuinely passed unit_tests ... the general partial required gate case stays open'; it also REJECTED 'let a post-merge full-suite pass settle partial gates'. Today a required gate recorded partial (baseline-red unit_tests, a partial_exits command) can only be passed by a genuine re-run, or by --force (all blockers; the hook blocks it for agents). Stranded merged-but-not-completed: fix-B1bfcaf6ebb, fix-Be305b7d6ea, fix-B-roborev-branch-arch-guards.

A tested prototype is on branch ddflow/fix-Bb999d5e20f (tests/test_accept_partial_gate.py, 5 tests): `ddflow approve <id> <gate>` by a PERSON accepts the ONE recorded partial outcome by digest via services.approval (refused under an agent identity, no MCP tool); the gate stays partial in the record; complete warns and verify notes it; a re-record needs a fresh acceptance; failed/unavailable cannot be accepted. The rubber_duck reviewer (deepseek) flagged it HIGH x3 as contradicting that decision for code items, so it is NOT merged.

OPTIONS (pick one; record it as a decision):
A. Person-accepted partial, as the prototype, for code items too (amends D-docs-gates-not-applicable: a person, not an agent, may accept a partial required gate; it is never turned into passed).
B. As A, behind a knob [gates].accept_partial (default off): the project opts in; costs a knob, README table, upgrade-manifest entry.
C. As A, restricted to a partial that is machine-measured baseline-red (every failing test also fails on the base, bug filed: gate_baseline.apply), not partial_exits or hand-recorded partials.
D. No new settle path: a genuine re-run once the base is green, or the operator runs complete --force from their own shell; only fix the blocker text to say so (smallest).
E. A post-merge full-suite pass on the base settles the partial (rejected 2026-10-19; listed for completeness).
Recommendation: C (narrowest honest case; a hand-recorded partial stays a re-run).
Note: fix-Bb999d5e20f's declared glob ddflow/api/complete* matches no file (the code is ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete.py and ddflow/services/completion.py).
data.title: Operator decision: how may a required gate recorded partial settle complete (Bb999d5e20f)?

data.text: Operator decision on Q-decide-partial-required-gate (AskUserQuestion 2026-10-21), option verbatim: 'C: person accepts only a baseline-red partial (Recommended)'

data.alternatives: A: any partial acceptable (too broad); B: knob default off; D: no new path (--force only); E: post-merge full-suite pass (rejected 2026-10-19).
data.context: Bug Bb999d5e20f: baseline-red partial gates stranded items merged-but-not-completed.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-21 (Q-decide-partial-required-gate, option C): a person (ddflow approve <id> <gate>; never an agent, no MCP tool) may accept a partial required gate ONLY when ddflow measured it as baseline-red (the failing tests also fail on the base branch: evidence baseline.red written by gate run). The gate stays partial in the record; complete warns it settled on that acceptance; failed, unavailable and hand-recorded or partial_exits partials cannot be accepted; a re-record or re-measure needs a fresh acceptance (digest of outcome, time, reason). Amends the partial-case wording of D-docs-gates-not-applicable: code items still need a passed unit_tests, except this one person-accepted baseline-red case.
data.title: A person may accept a required gate's partial only when ddflow measured it baseline-red

chunk_findings.detail: `_accepted_warnings` does not exclude gates listed in `s.not_applicable` the way `_unsettled` does. A required gate that has become not_applicable (for example, an item whose only changed files are now docs, so `unit_tests` is not_applicable) can still carry an earlier `GA.ACCEPTABLE` (partial) outcome and an acceptance record. `_unsettled` correctly removes that gate from `missing` due to the `g not in s.not_applicable` check, but `_accepted_warnings` then sees `g in required and g not in missing and it.gate_outcome(g) == GA.ACCEPTABLE` and, if `GA.accepted(state, it, g).ok` is true from the stale acceptance, appends a warning claiming the gate “settles only because a person accepted that outcome” when it actually settles because the gate is not_applicable. This produces a false and misleading warning for such items.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion.py:_accepted_warnings

chunk_findings.detail: `refusal` decides whether a partial was measured baseline-red by reading `(it.gates[gate].evidence or {}).get("baseline")`, but the evidence recorded by `gate run` is named `baseline.red` as stated in this file’s own docstring and in [D-accept-baseline-red-partial] (“evidence baseline.red written by gate run”). Given a legitimate `unit_tests` record with `outcome == "partial"` and `evidence == {"baseline.red": True}`, `.get("baseline")` returns `None`, the `isinstance(base, dict) and base.get("red") is True` check fails, and `refusal()` refuses the acceptance with “partial but was not measured baseline-red”. Therefore `grant()` raises `ValueError` and `accepted()` returns False even after the required person approval, so the bug is not fixed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:refusal

chunk_findings.detail: `_accepted_warnings` asserts a gate `settles only because a person accepted that outcome`, but it determines “only because” by checking only `g not in missing`. `g not in missing` is also true when `_unsettled` excludes the gate via `CO.skipped_ok(cfg, it, excused, g)` -- i.e. the actual diff already excuses it. Given a required gate that the actual diff excuses but whose stored record is still an accepted partial (for example an item reworked to a docs-only actual diff after a baseline-red partial was accepted), `complete` will emit a warning claiming it settled only because a person accepted it, which is false. It should pass/check the same `CO.skipped_ok`/excuse guard before emitting that warning.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion.py:_accepted_warnings

chunk_findings.detail: `refusal()` still reads `(it.gates[gate].evidence or {}).get("baseline")` and requires `{"baseline": {"red": True}}`, but [D-accept-baseline-red-partial] and this file’s own docstring state that `gate run` writes the evidence key `baseline.red`. A legitimate baseline-red partial record (`it.gate_outcome(gate) == "partial"`, `evidence == {"baseline.red": True}`) returns the refusal message “not measured baseline-red”, so `accepted()` returns false and `grant()` raises; the person-permitted acceptance path from the operator decision is therefore unusable for the exact evidence the decision says `gate run` writes. The cited prior probe does not answer this because the defect is the evidence key itself, not a fixture that models the nested `{"baseline": {...}}` shape.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:refusal

chunk_findings.detail: `_partial_item(repo)` simulates the real `gate run` measurement by appending `"evidence": BASELINE`, where `BASELINE = {"baseline": {"red": True, ...}}`. But the acceptance logic (and this file’s own `test_the_evidence_gate_run_writes_is_what_acceptance_reads` docstring, plus [D-accept-baseline-red-partial]) requires the gate-run evidence key `"baseline.red"`. With the corrected `gate_accept.refusal`, `{"baseline": {...}}` is not recognized as a ddflow-measured baseline-red partial, so the simulated partial is refused. Concretely, `test_a_person_can_accept_a_partial_required_gate_and_complete_follows` calls `run_cli(repo, "approve", "T1", "unit_tests", ...)` after `_partial_item(repo)` and asserts success, but approval will fail because the simulated evidence is mis-keyed. The prior triage probe only ran `-k evidence_gate_run`; that test calls `GB.apply` directly and never exercises this fixture, so it does not expose the contradiction.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_accept_partial_gate.py:33 (`BASELINE`, used by `_remeasure`)

evidence.note: ruff check+format clean; python -m ddflow.services.roborev_branch: No issues found (2 low observations: theoretical forgery -> test_a_caller_cannot_forge_the_measurement_through_gate_record added)

chunk_findings.detail: `accepted` receives `state` but never consults `state.not_applicable`, and `refusal` does not either. A docs-only item whose `unit_tests` is recorded `not_applicable` can still carry an earlier `partial` gate record with `evidence.baseline.red is True`; `gate_accept.grant` will record an acceptance and `gate_accept.accepted` will return true for it. That violates [D-accept-baseline-red-partial], which allows accepting only a required gate, and it is the same not_applicable edge from the previous finding: the gate is not required, so it must not be accepted or warned as settled by acceptance.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:accepted

chunk_findings.detail: `_accepted` only checks `GA.accepted(...).ok`; it never excludes gates in `st.not_applicable`. A docs-only item whose `unit_tests` is `not_applicable` with a reason and also has an earlier partial acceptance record will therefore be returned as `accepted`. `_gates` then appends `"partial, accepted by a person (still not passed)"` and returns WARN, even though the gate is not applicable and `complete` should not mention it as an accepted partial. This is the same not_applicable gap as the previously confirmed `_accepted_warnings` bug, now in the new `_gates` warning path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify.py:262 (_accepted)

chunk_findings.detail: The acceptance predicate reads `(it.gates[gate].evidence or {}).get("baseline")` and requires `{"baseline": {"red": True}}`. [D-accept-baseline-red-partial] records the real `gate run` evidence as the dotted key `"baseline.red"` (`evidence == {"baseline.red": True}`), and this diff does not change the `baseline_red` writer. A legitimate baseline-red partial record therefore gets the refusal message “not measured baseline-red”; `accepted()` returns false and `grant()` raises for the exact case this change is meant to allow. The previous refutation’s probe only runs `tests/test_accept_partial_gate.py`; the previous finding on that test notes the simulated `gate run` evidence is itself constructed as `{"baseline": {"red": True, ...}}`, so the probe only checks the code against its own chosen shape and cannot catch a mismatch with the real `gate run` evidence key.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:refusal

chunk_findings.detail: This test does not actually exercise a forged valid baseline-red measurement. The decision [D-accept-baseline-red-partial] and the sibling test `test_the_evidence_gate_run_writes_is_what_acceptance_reads` say the real gate-run evidence key is `{"baseline.red": true}`, but the forged JSON supplied here is `'{"baseline": {"red": true}}'` (nested `baseline`). A correct refusal can reject that input purely because the shape is wrong, even if the implementation would accept a caller-supplied `{"baseline.red": true}`. The ignored exit code of the `gate record --evidence` call makes it worse: if the CLI rejects the argument and records nothing, the subsequent `approve` fails because `_partial_item(..., baseline=False)` already left a non-baseline partial. The test should assert the forged record now carries the real `baseline.red` shape before expecting `approve` to fail.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_accept_partial_gate.py:test_a_caller_cannot_forge_the_measurement_through_gate_record

chunk_findings.detail: This still holds from the earlier confirmed finding: `accepted(state, it, gate)` never consults `state` (in particular `state.not_applicable` or the current required-gate set), and `grant` has no `state` parameter at all. `refusal` only checks `it.gate_outcome(gate) == "partial"` and `it.gates[gate].evidence["baseline"]["red"] is True`, so a docs-only item whose `unit_tests` is recorded not-applicable but which still has an earlier baseline-red partial record can have `gate_accept.grant` record an acceptance and `gate_accept.accepted` return a true verdict. That violates [D-accept-baseline-red-partial], which allows accepting only a required gate's partial. Concrete input: `state.not_applicable = {"unit_tests": "docs-only"}`, `it.gates["unit_tests"]` is partial with `evidence={"baseline": {"red": True}}`; `accepted(state, it, "unit_tests")` returns true once the approval exists.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:accepted/grant

chunk_findings.detail: The new accept path for non-human gates checks only `it.gate_outcome(gate) == GA.ACCEPTABLE` and never consults `it.not_applicable`. A docs-only item can first have a baseline-red partial `unit_tests` record and later record `unit_tests` as not-applicable under the docs-gates decision; `gate_outcome("unit_tests")` still matches `GA.ACCEPTABLE`, so `ddflow approve <id> unit_tests` calls `GA.grant` and returns `partial outcome ACCEPTED...`. That leaves the gate both not-applicable and accepted partial. This is the same not-applicable gap from the confirmed previous finding on `gate_accept.accepted`/`refusal`, now reachable through this new command entrypoint, and violates [D-accept-baseline-red-partial].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/outcomes.py:approve (non-human gate branch)

chunk_findings.detail: The new not-applicable related test only calls `completion._accepted_warnings` directly with a hand-built `SimpleNamespace` that carries `not_applicable`. It never exercises `gate_accept.accepted` or `verify._accepted`, the functions previous review identified as not consulting `state.not_applicable`. So a docs-only item whose `unit_tests` is recorded `not_applicable` and also has an earlier accepted partial record can still make `GA.accepted(...)` return true and `verify._accepted` report `"accepted by a person"` while this test still passes; the regression suite does not fail on the confirmed not-applicable edge.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_accept_partial_gate.py:151 test_a_gate_the_diff_made_not_applicable_gets_no_acceptance_warning

chunk_findings.detail: The test still does not exercise a forged valid baseline-red measurement. The real gate-run evidence key is `{"baseline.red": true}` (as asserted by the sibling test `test_the_evidence_gate_run_writes_is_what_acceptance_reads`), but the forged JSON supplied here is the nested shape `{"baseline": {"red": true}}`. A correct refusal can reject that input purely because the evidence shape is wrong, so the test would still pass even if `gate_accept.refusal` accepted a caller-supplied `{"baseline.red": true}`. The earlier triage marked this finding `confirmed`, and the submitted change does not answer it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_accept_partial_gate.py:test_a_caller_cannot_forge_the_measurement_through_gate_record

chunk_findings.detail: The acceptance check reads `(it.gates[gate].evidence or {}).get("baseline")` and requires `{"baseline": {"red": True}}`, but the governing decision [D-accept-baseline-red-partial] states that the gate runner records the real baseline-red evidence under the dotted key `"baseline.red"`.
